source.title: PirateNets: Physics-informed Deep Learning with Residual Adaptive Networks
source.authors: Sifan Wang; Bowen Li; Yuhan Chen; Paris Perdikaris

record.file_problem: Full text is present; minor transcription/formatting artifacts, but no relevant truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests depth and initialization effects on PINN trainability in PDE tasks, an application setting different from the claim's CIFAR classification benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The study reports PDE relative L2 errors and training convergence, not classification error. Figure-only depth values are recorded as figure only; the text describes the overall trends. Cited results from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study investigates PINN optimization, but its results do not measure any listed version. V3 concerns training error in batch-normalized convolutional classifiers; these rows measure PDE solution prediction error in tanh MLP and residual backbones. V4 concerns initialization that preserves signals and gradients in plain networks; the study's initialization comparisons concern adaptive residual networks or data-fitted output layers, while its plain-MLP analysis measures input derivatives rather than optimization gradients.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute poor deep-PINN trainability to pathological initialization of MLP input derivatives and propose adaptive residual networks initialized as shallow models. They report improved optimization and prediction accuracy across PDE benchmarks. Their PDE error estimates and derivative analysis support this explanation, but do not establish that initialization is the sole cause of the observed failures.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies PINN optimization for PDE solution approximation, using Adam and residual/adaptive architectures; the claim versions concern classification training or specific image and toy-network setups.
record.method_sensitivity: Backbone architecture and depth change the reported prediction-error trend: MLP error rises, ResNet error rises more slowly, and PirateNet error falls as depth increases.

fits_no_version.finding: On Allen-Cahn, MLP prediction error increases with depth, reaching nearly 100% at 18 hidden layers; conventional residual connections slow the increase, while PirateNet prediction error decreases with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested PINN recipe, increasing depth degrades PDE solution accuracy for conventional MLP and residual backbones, while adaptive residual PirateNets benefit from depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 3 bounds initial first-input-derivative variance by inverse width for Glorot-initialized tanh MLPs. Figure 2 reports shrinking derivative variance with width and poorer sinusoid approximation by higher-order derivative networks at greater depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard initialization can produce poorly varying input derivatives and difficult derivative-network optimization in PINNs; these quantities differ from the signal and optimization-gradient preservation named in V4.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 10 and 13 compare the same PirateNet architecture with residual coefficients initialized at zero or one. Zero initialization improves Grey-Scott prediction accuracy by one or two orders of magnitude; on Ginzburg-Landau, initialization at one causes deeper models to collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initializing adaptive residual PINNs as identity blocks can improve depth scalability relative to initializing their blocks as fully nonlinear.

record.problems: The directly relevant depth comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values in the text. Results concern PDE prediction error, not classification error, and use five random seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows within the 60-row limit were required for the mapped depth comparison. Other PDE benchmark scores and ablations concern general PINN performance or architecture components rather than a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size, stopping or regularization comparisons.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on student overwidth.
Depth-dependent training error in plain batch-normalized convolutional classifiers and prevention by identity shortcuts; longer-training controls and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation improving plain-network training speed or trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep orthogonal convolutional networks.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, loss recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. No verdict follows merely from using Glorot initialization or residual connections. The cannot_determine states concern the listed versions, not whether the reported PINN depth trends exist. Exact figure-only values cannot be recovered from the supplied text. Additional PINN ablations fit no listed version, so they are not missing version-bearing rows.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and stopping or regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Batch-normalized convolutional image classifiers, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, and training classification error. This paper tests PINN prediction error as depth varies for MLP, ResNet, and PirateNet backbones.

Activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks. The paper examines Glorot-initialized MLP derivatives and PirateNet's adaptive residual initialization in PINNs.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization and training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

reader_labels.condition: Allen-Cahn PINNs using MLP, ResNet, or PirateNet backbones
reader_labels.reason: Depth worsens MLP prediction error; conventional residual connections slow but do not eliminate the trend, while PirateNet improves with depth (R1–R18). This is a PDE prediction-error extension, not the version's classification-error setting.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Allen-Cahn PINNs with PirateNet adaptive residual initialization
reader_labels.reason: The tested PirateNet improves in relative L2 prediction error as depth increases (R13–R18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Allen-Cahn PINNs with conventional MLP initialization
reader_labels.reason: Deeper MLPs show increasing prediction error, with near-total failure at 18 hidden layers (R1–R6).
